summary.headline: IRM Energy FY26 revenue rose 9% to INR 1,066.66 crore and EBITDA 17% to INR 112.25 crore; management guides FY27 volume above 250 MMSCM.
summary.overview: FY26 volume reached 223.67 MMSCM (+9% YoY), with PAT of INR 56.89 crore (+21% YoY, standalone) and CNG stations crossing 150 (up from 111). Q4 PBT was about INR 17.7 crore against INR 22 crore in Q3, as management attributed INR 4.2 crore of one-time items (JV receivable provision INR 1.34 crore and bank charges INR 2.86 crore) to the decline and said both would be reversed or resolved in Q1 FY27. Gas sourcing was disrupted after the Gulf conflict, with Fatehgarh Sahib industrial supply cut to 55-65% of contracts before recovering to 80%. Management guided to gross margin and per-SCM EBITDA improvement of 10-15% and double-digit volume growth in FY27.

segments.name: CNG
segments.commentary: Largest contributor at 61% of FY26 operational revenue; station network reached 150 (from 111, +26% YoY) with 39 added in FY26 and 36 targeted in FY27. About 40% of CNG volume is sourced from APM/NWG gas, with HPHT gas for the balance; management says 4% of CNG was spot purchase in FY26.

segments.name: PNG Domestic
segments.commentary: Added 83,262 domestic connections in FY26; Diu and Gir Somnath has crossed 10,000 domestic PNG connections.

segments.name: PNG Commercial and Industrial
segments.commentary: Added 496 commercial and 223 industrial connections in FY26. Industrial volume is affected by the Fatehgarh Sahib NGT order and gas cuts; management expects industrial growth of 23-24% in FY27 if the order is implemented.

segments.name: GA-wise: Banaskantha (Gujarat)
segments.commentary: About 49% of FY26 revenue and 47% of volume, with about INR 420 crore invested; CNG-centric with higher margins.

segments.name: GA-wise: Fatehgarh Sahib (Punjab)
segments.commentary: About 36% of FY26 revenue (mainly industrial PNG) and 39% of volume, with about INR 200 crore invested.

segments.name: GA-wise: Namakkal and Trichy (Tamil Nadu)
segments.commentary: About INR 257 crore gross block invested to date; FY27 capex planned at INR 150-180 crore. Management expects around 90% CNG volume mix initially, moving toward 70:20 CNG to PNG over one to two years. 71 TNSTC PNG buses running with 50 more due in May 2026.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth expected at 30%+ over FY26 in management's words, with volume crossing 250 MMSCM 'or maybe much more'; the CEO also said 'double-digit' growth, and the CFO said 14-15% was not out of line.
EBITDA per SCM to improve 10-15% in FY27 from current levels of more than INR 5 per SCM; CFO guided to INR 5.3-5.5 per SCM.
Gross margin and EBITDA margin expected to be maintained in the 25-26% gross margin range, subject to how the Gulf situation unfolds.
Peak debt for FY27 expected at INR 70-80 crore, against about INR 49 crore of term loans at end March 2026 and a INR 45 crore sanctioned term loan.
Namakkal and Trichy capex funded from IPO proceeds (about INR 194 crore available at end March 2026); other GAs funded from internal accruals plus the term loan.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex INR 184.35 crore, including INR 81.33 crore in Q4 FY26 alone.
Cumulative investment to date: Banaskantha about INR 420 crore, Fatehgarh Sahib about INR 200 crore, Namakkal and Trichy INR 257 crore gross block.
FY27 target: 36 new CNG stations (39 added in FY26); Namakkal and Trichy capex of INR 150-180 crore.
Network of 6,695 inch-km pipeline as of FY26; about 35% of the cascade fleet is Type 3 cylinders. Trichy bus stand CNG station planned.
First LNG dispensing facility commissioned at Rasipuram (Namakkal and Trichy GA).
demand_pricing: Gas cost pressure from APM ceiling rising to USD 7/MMBTU (from USD 6.75) and higher NWG-linked prices; management says the increase was passed through to CNG, industrial and commercial customers from April.
HPHT gas price via IGX reduced from USD 9.72 to USD 8.92 per MMBTU, offsetting some cost pressure.
CNG sales for April 2026 were in line with budget after the price pass-through, per management.
Fatehgarh Sahib industrial supply cut to 80%, then 65% and 55% of contracted quantity during the Gulf disruption, now restored to 80%; demand destruction is occurring in industrial.

Namakkal and Trichy: CNG demand nearly doubled YoY after the OMC CNG model rollout; 92-95% of new three-wheeler sales are CNG; CNG share of passenger vehicle additions above 15% in that GA (vs over 40% in Banaskantha).
Management says EV penetration in its GAs is negligible; CNG auto and taxi demand continues to grow.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for FY27 given the Gulf crisis and sourcing?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: gross margin of 25-26% has risen YoY; management expects margins to hold in that range, depending on how the situation unfolds.

qa_highlights.question: Why did profit fall from Q3 to Q4 FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a INR 1.34 crore JV receivable provision (Ni Hon Cylinders) and a INR 2.86 crore bank charge, both expected to reverse in Q1 FY27. The analyst noted PBT of about INR 17.7 crore in Q4 vs INR 22 crore in Q3, still a gap after adding back these items.

qa_highlights.question: When will the NGT order for Fatehgarh Sahib be implemented?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is not pushing for immediate enforcement given demand destruction and gas cuts; it will press PPCB and CPCB once supply stabilises.

qa_highlights.question: Guidance for FY27 volume and EBITDA per SCM?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth expected above 30% (to above 250 MMSCM); EBITDA per SCM to rise 10-15% from current levels of more than INR 5.

qa_highlights.question: How much CNG is spot-sourced?
qa_highlights.answer: Only about 4% of CNG volume was spot purchase in FY26; about 40% comes from APM/NWG gas, and the rest from long-term contracts and HPHT bids.

qa_highlights.question: What funds the Namakkal and Trichy capex?
qa_highlights.answer: IPO proceeds of about INR 194 crore at end March 2026; other GAs are funded through internal accruals and a term loan.

qa_highlights.question: What is the treasury income and cash flow treatment?
qa_highlights.answer: Treasury income from liquid and overnight funds was about INR 68 lakh in Q4 FY26, per management, versus about INR 2 crore cited by the analyst as the quarter figure.

risks_watch: Gas sourcing: APM ceiling increase, NWG price rise and Gulf supply disruption could pressure margins if pass-through slows; management says CNG and domestic are insulated.
Fatehgarh Sahib industrial volumes: NGT-linked restrictions, demand destruction and gas cuts; implementation timing is uncertain.
Q1 FY27 must show reversal of the INR 1.34 crore JV provision and INR 2.86 crore bank charge, as management stated.
Execution of 36 CNG station additions and INR 150-180 crore Namakkal and Trichy capex; the new Tamil Nadu government's policy stance was flagged as a source of difficulty.
Employee cost rise (headcount from 214 to 256) and a INR 60 lakh labour code provision; license fee at 2% of net revenue.
Management declined to give firm numeric guidance, citing an evolving situation; several outlook figures were given as ranges and 'maybe' targets.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the FY26 operating record and the CNG and network expansion, but cautious on near-term guidance, which management described as hard to predict given the Gulf disruption. Management was defensive when questioned on the Q4 profit decline, attributing it to one-time items, and gave a hedged, range-based outlook.
key_quotes: So the gross margins that we see, they are in the range of 25% to 26%. They have increased from previous year.
We are expecting that in all four segments, we will be growing more than 20% year-on-year.
CNG remains the largest contributor to the volume, accounting for 61% of total operational revenue in FY'26.

growth.why: FY27 volume guided to cross 250 MMSCM (30%+ growth per management, though CEO also said double-digit and CFO 14-15%), backed by 36 new CNG stations, INR 150-180 crore Namakkal/Trichy capex and IPO-funded build-out, but industrial demand is shrinking and gas supply was cut to 55% of contracts during the Gulf disruption, so backing is partial.
